report:
Freshly reviewed the current claim, full compile/mod.rs implementation snapshot, complete two-test association set, and additionally captured Cargo.toml. There is one ordinary implementation association (compile_test macro) and two ordinary tests; no TODO/N/A deferrals. The claim requires ordinary Rust/Cargo test execution, fixture expressions and explicit call-site expect values, reuse of sage::test associations without custom discovery, and propagation of failed observations as test failures.
The macro expands synchronously to a block constructing CompileTest, dispatching expr-valued fields, and calling run. Both source and files accept source expressions, with source accepting AsRef<str>. The expectation setters take Expect directly; run passes prepared observation/diagnostic/query strings to the supplied expectation assert_eq methods. Preparation errors panic, and assertion failures are not caught. No custom registration or test harness is introduced. The captured manifest leaves Cargo test discovery and harness enabled by default. The essential invocation entry and failure propagation are in the associated implementation file; downstream observation semantics are separate claims.
call_argument_types is an ordinary #[test] with the existing sage::test association. Its visible macro call accepts an indoc source expression, explicit inline expectations for the function path, literal argument and call-result types, and empty diagnostics. This provides meaningful positive coverage of both expression input and call-site assertions. blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates constructs a disposable normal Cargo package and a plain #[test] calling compile_test. The visible run closure invokes cargo test and compares its exit status. The stale observation is required to fail without UPDATE_EXPECT and the output must specifically contain 'expect test failed', distinguishing observation failure from a build error. The fixture remains unchanged on failure. The subsequent explicit update requires precise observed text to appear once, and a final run with updates disabled must pass. These assertions catch swallowed expectation failures or bypassed macro execution. The unexpected rustc diagnostic branch separately requires a failed Rust test and unchanged source even in update mode. Blessing behavior is an explicit mode covered by its own claim; it does not obscure the normal-mode failure assertion here. No separate discovery or anchor attribute occurs in either call site.
All requirements have concrete current source and test assertions. No suspected behavioral defect or missing evidence was found, and no source edits are requested. This refresh is a source adequacy assessment: I executed review start/read/record commands, not behavior tests; the coordinator is running tests centrally. Earlier test results or approvals are not used as execution evidence for this refresh.
